crapper_portrait.title: Thomas Crapper.jpg
crapper_portrait.caption: Thomas Crapper, the Victorian sanitary engineer
crapper_portrait.desc: Square photo, three-quarter-length seated portrait on a light background (about 23% near-white). Face detected just left of centre, about 28% down (upper third).

crapper_cistern.title: Thomas Crapper Toilet Horta Museum cistern.jpg
crapper_cistern.caption: A Thomas Crapper cistern at the Horta Museum, Brussels (modern photograph)
crapper_cistern.desc: Landscape photo of a wall-mounted cistern; detail concentrated upper left, so the cistern likely sits upper left to centre. Framing is a guess from the edge map.

crapper_waste_preventer.title: Crapper's Valveless Waste Preventer.jpg
crapper_waste_preventer.caption: Crapper's 'Valveless Waste Preventer No. 814', a cistern patented by Thomas Crapper
crapper_waste_preventer.desc: Vertical photo, fairly dark, detail spread evenly; the cast cistern and its lettering likely fill the centre. A guess from the edge map.

crapper_manhole.title: A genuine Crapper - geograph.org.uk - 108112.jpg
crapper_manhole.caption: A Crapper manhole cover in Faversham, Kent: 'T Crapper & Co Sanitary Engineers, Marlboro Works, Chelsea, London'
crapper_manhole.desc: Small (640 x 470) shot of a cast-iron cover filling the frame, lettering around the centre. Low resolution: keep it small or the push-in gentle.

crapper_grave.title: Beckenham Cemetery 20181022 133700 (45494456541).jpg
crapper_grave.caption: Thomas Crapper's grave, Beckenham Cemetery, London (modern photograph)
crapper_grave.desc: Landscape photo; detail strongest centre-left and middle, gravestone likely centre. A guess from the edge map.

knossos_drain.title: Drainage System and gypsum blocks, Knossos, 144442.jpg
knossos_drain.caption: Stone drainage channels at the palace of Knossos, Crete (modern photograph)
knossos_drain.desc: Landscape ruins photo, no border; detail strongest left and top-right, the drain channel likely runs through the left-centre (a guess).

knossos_royal_drain.title: Knossos Königliche Gemächer Abfluss 01.jpg
knossos_royal_drain.caption: A drain leading from the royal apartments at Knossos (modern photograph)
knossos_royal_drain.desc: Landscape close-up of stonework, detail even across the frame; drain likely centre.

knossos_queens_megaron.title: Queen's Megaron, Knossos, 144473.jpg
knossos_queens_megaron.caption: The Queen's Megaron, part of the private quarters of the palace at Knossos (modern photograph)
knossos_queens_megaron.desc: Landscape view of the restored room, detail even across the frame, slightly stronger right; centre composition.

knossos_ruins.title: Ruins on Crete, Knossos. Center of Minoan civilization. Castle with flush toilets, sewage system, water piped in from 7 miles away LOC matpc.23191.jpg
knossos_ruins.credit: G. Eric and Edith Matson Photograph Collection / Library of Congress / Wikimedia Commons
knossos_ruins.caption: The ruins of the palace of Knossos, Crete (Matson Collection photograph, 1950s-70s)
knossos_ruins.desc: Landscape colour slide with a narrow edge (about 2%); quiet sky across the top third, ruins in the middle and lower bands, densest lower right.

knossos_evans_plan.title: The palace of Minos - a comparative account of the successive stages of the early Cretan civilization as illustrated by the discoveries at Knossos (1921) (14587028407).jpg
knossos_evans_plan.credit: Arthur Evans, The Palace of Minos (1921) / Internet Archive Book Images / Wikimedia Commons
knossos_evans_plan.caption: Plans and sections of the Knossos palace drains, from Arthur Evans's The Palace of Minos (1921)
knossos_evans_plan.desc: Tall book illustration, about 84% white: line plans and sections. Identified from the scanned page text around it (Fig. 170-171, 'Drainage and Sanitary System'), so treat the subject as likely, not certain.

mohenjo_daro.title: Mohenjo-daro.jpg
mohenjo_daro.caption: Mohenjo-daro in the Indus Valley: the Great Bath in front, the granary mound behind (modern photograph)
mohenjo_daro.desc: Landscape; pale sky across the top band (about 13%), ruins across the middle; the Great Bath in the foreground per Commons, centre to lower centre.

mohenjo_street.title: Street - Mohenjodaro.JPG
mohenjo_street.caption: A street of brick buildings at Mohenjo-daro (modern photograph)
mohenjo_street.desc: Vertical; sky in the top 16%, brick walls and street through the middle and lower frame; street likely recedes through the centre.

lothal_drain.title: Lothal Drainage System.jpg
lothal_drain.caption: Brick drains at Lothal, another Indus Valley city (modern photograph)
lothal_drain.desc: Wide landscape; detail strongest in the lower third and at left, so the drains run across the lower half.

harington_portrait.title: Portrait of Sir John Harington of Kelston (1561–1612).jpg
harington_portrait.credit: Attributed to Hieronimo Custodis, 1592 / Wikimedia Commons
harington_portrait.caption: Sir John Harington, who built a flushing toilet with a cistern for Elizabeth I (portrait dated 1592)
harington_portrait.desc: Dark three-quarter-length painting, no border. Face detected centre-right, about 17% down (top third). Face position from detection on a thumbnail.

ajax_title.title: Sir J. Harington, A new discourse... Wellcome M0012964.jpg
ajax_title.caption: The Metamorphosis of Ajax: the title page, 'A New Discourse of a Stale Subject' (British Museum copy)
ajax_title.desc: Vertical book page, mostly white (about 81%); printed block in the left four-fifths and top nine-tenths; centre of interest a little left of centre.

ajax_diagram.title: Sir J. Harington, Diagram of the water-closet Wellcome M0012969.jpg
ajax_diagram.caption: Harington's diagram of his water closet, from The Metamorphosis of Ajax (1596)
ajax_diagram.desc: Landscape scan of an open book spread, about half white; detail spread evenly across both pages, so the diagram likely spans the centre. Exact layout is a guess.

ajax_description.title: Sir J. Harington,The description of the water-closet Wellcome M0012968.jpg
ajax_description.caption: Harington's printed description of his water closet, The Metamorphosis of Ajax (1596)
ajax_description.desc: Landscape scan of a two-page spread of text (about 64% white); text blocks left and right of centre.

elizabeth_i.title: Elizabeth I Armada Portrait British School.jpg
elizabeth_i.credit: Unknown artist, British School, about 1588 / Wikimedia Commons
elizabeth_i.caption: Queen Elizabeth I (the 'Armada Portrait', about 1588)
elizabeth_i.desc: Near-square painting, no border. Queen's face detected centre, about 22% down (upper third); a second detection lower right is probably a false hit.

cumming_sbend.title: Cummings S-bend.jpg
cumming_sbend.caption: Alexander Cumming's 1775 patent drawing of his water closet with the S-bend
cumming_sbend.desc: Tiny (355 x 355) line drawing on white (about 81% blank), drawing centred. Use small on a card, no push-in.

wc_engravings.title: Eight illustrations of water closets and pipework. Engraving Wellcome V0020280.jpg
wc_engravings.credit: Mutlow and Russell / Wellcome Collection / Wikimedia Commons
wc_engravings.caption: Engraved diagrams of water closets and pipework (Mutlow and Russell; date not recorded)
wc_engravings.desc: Vertical engraved plate of eight diagrams, no big border; detail even, slightly stronger centre. Diagrams only.
